summary: Close to implementable, with the core CAS, tree construction and result types fully specified; the biggest gap is the exact path selection for the overlap check and post-CAS synchronization, including what happens to workspace files that are not exported.

questions.text: Do the overlap check and post-CAS synchronization cover the whole replaced subtree prefixes or only the paths whose content actually changed?
questions.reason: Decides which local edits refuse acceptance or get overwritten; the ADR says 'synchronize the paths written or removed by this acceptance' but its replacements and restore command operate on whole subtrees.

questions.text: How should synchronization treat live workspace files that ExportAcceptedWorkspace does not export, such as saved candidates or evaluation results?
questions.reason: If they sit inside the synced prefix, every acceptance reports WorkingTreeUpdateIncomplete; the ADR retains untracked files as incomplete but leaves where saved material lives to EvolutionStore/ADR 0010.

questions.text: What counts as 'stale' material for InvalidMaterial, and are edited inputs reported as InvalidMaterial by the application or as WorkspaceChanged by publication?
questions.reason: Fixes which layer checks captured inputs and which refusal and repair advice tests assert; the ADR lists 'missing, stale or rejected' as InvalidMaterial and defines WorkspaceChanged separately without separating them.

questions.text: What CLI exit status does an accepted commit with WorkingTreeUpdateIncomplete (and the matching initialization result) produce?
questions.reason: Scripts must distinguish accepted-but-needs-repair from success and refusal; the ADR only says NotReady exits non-zero and that sync failure must not hide acceptance.

questions.text: In what order are the publication refusals (checkout, base, workspace, overlap) checked, and which one is reported when several apply?
questions.reason: NotAccepted carries one problem with distinct repair advice; the ADR only fixes that readiness is checked first, in the application layer.

questions.text: Which component resolves CommitMetadata identity and date for acceptance and initialization, from what source, and at what point relative to the readiness check?
questions.reason: Affects signatures and refusal ordering; the ADR says the caller supplies metadata, yet also requires refusal 'before commit-identity lookup' and treats missing identity as an initialization preflight refusal.

questions.text: Where does the LocalBranch come from when the caller names none: always the checked-out branch, or an optional flag or persisted setting?
questions.reason: Decides adapter resolution order and whether CheckoutMismatch is a routine refusal; the ADR says the branch is not a mandatory persisted configuration and proposes the checked-out branch.
